_doc: Example limits for gate.mjs. kinds.<idle|walk|run|move>.<checkId> is {max}, {min}, {min,max} or {equals}; a check with no limit here is not run. heroes.<id>.<kind>.<checkId> overrides one check for one hero (null switches it off); <id> is the metrics' 'char'. These values were calibrated on one game's accepted captures at 1600x900, 30 fps, about 0.55 screen px per skeleton unit, unlit: every px limit is in those screen pixels, so recalibrate on clips you have accepted by eye at your own capture size before trusting them. references/gate.md explains each check, which limits carry over, and how to set them for a first hero.

example-tank._note: An example of per-hero baselines, from a shield-and-hammer tank hero. Hole limits are the silhouette's own painted gaps, each named: idle 310 (the gap between the hammer arm and the coat); walk 460 (that gap opened by the march, plus the pocket between the far shin and the shield); run 250 (the arm-coat gap opened by the arm's pump); move 3100 (one real opening of one move, under the far forearm between the coat, the shield's inner edge and the far leg stepping in). A crack is never a reason to raise a limit.

example-rifle._note: An example of a loosened and a switched-off check. Walk slide 4: the step-drag walk the human picked by eye moves the sole bone about 3.4 px while planted. Move box check off: several old clips draw past the box and nobody has judged them yet; judge them, then fix the box or the clip and drop this.
